title: Markdown: code-fence-aware headings, slugs, and a generated table of contents
prompt:
This repository is a small Python Markdown toolkit (`mdtools/`) with unittest tests in `tests/` (run them with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`). Add a table-of-contents generator, keeping the existing tests passing and adding tests of your own.

1. Fix `parse_headings` in `mdtools/headings.py`: lines inside fenced code blocks are not headings. A fence opens with a line starting with three or more backticks or tildes (after up to three spaces of indentation) and closes with a line of at least as many of the same character. An unclosed fence runs to the end of the document. Also strip an optional closing sequence of `#` characters that is preceded by a space (`## Title ##` has the text `Title`).
2. New module `mdtools/slug.py`:
   - `slugify(text)` makes a GitHub-style anchor: lowercase; remove every character that is not a letter, digit, space, hyphen or underscore; then replace each space with a hyphen. Leading and trailing whitespace is removed first. Example: `slugify("Hello, World! 2.0")` is `hello-world-20`.
   - `SlugRegistry` with `unique(text)`: returns `slugify(text)` the first time a slug is seen and `<slug>-1`, `<slug>-2`, ... for repeats.
3. New module `mdtools/toc.py`:
   - `build_toc(text, min_level=2, max_level=3)` returns the table of contents as Markdown: one line `- [Heading text](#slug)` per heading with `min_level <= level <= max_level`, indented by two spaces per level below `min_level`, joined with `\n` and no trailing newline. Slugs are made with one `SlugRegistry` over all headings of the document in order, including those outside the level range, so anchors match what GitHub renders.
   - `insert_toc(text, min_level=2, max_level=3)` returns `text` with everything between a line `<!-- toc -->` and a line `<!-- tocstop -->` replaced by the table of contents (the marker lines stay, each on its own line, with the table of contents on the lines between them). Raise `ValueError` if either marker is missing.
4. New CLI command in `mdtools/cli.py`: `toc FILE [--min N] [--max N] [--in-place]`. Without `--in-place` it prints the table of contents; with it, it rewrites FILE with `insert_toc` and prints nothing. A missing marker prints `error: <message>` to stderr and returns exit code 1.

Use only the standard library.
